key_insight: An Abaqus implementation incorporates material strength into phase-field fracture and uses staggered solution updates to model brittle crack nucleation and propagation.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can simulate isotropic brittle fracture in Abaqus using elastic properties, tensile and compressive strengths, and fracture toughness as material inputs.
method: Use UMAT to exploit the heat-equation analogy, treating the strength-dependent phase-field driving force as a heat source.
Coordinate staggered displacement and phase-field solves with UEXTERNALDB, UAMP, MPC, and URDFIL.
Enforce phase-field bounds and irreversibility through a primal-dual active set approach.
evidence_signal: The implementation is demonstrated on silicate glass using the “Nine Circles of Elastic Brittle Fracture” tests, including simulations with CPS3, CAX3, and C3D4 elements.
watch_item: The presented formulation is limited to isotropic, linear-elastic brittle materials with a Drucker–Prager strength surface and requires coordinated user subroutines.
paper_title: Abaqus implementation of the phase-field approach to fracture
